summary: Master has not made this moot: _splitkv_gate needs 1 < batch, so full decode_1 still runs unpaired FA3 at 27.9 us (main 14.5, combine 7.0, pre-attn 1.3, plus prepare and rms_norm_gate). Reusing the proven fused batch-1 kernel there is a sound idea and the result reads directly from one shape. Because this is a scored submit and no test reaches the path, the implementer should add an import-time self-check with a fallback, and should not run the 64-way combine as a serial runtime loop.
justification: The mechanism is plausible. At batch 1 the full layer costs 27.9 us against a 4.3 us floor. About 10 us of that is FA3 combine plus prepare plus separate launches, and the fused kernel removes it, as it did on sliding decode_1 (16.6 -> 13.1 us). The masking change is correct against reference.py. seq_lens is the count of old tokens, positions = seq_lens + j, and the reference attends keys_past at 0..seq-1 plus the new entries. So FULL means lo = 0 and valid = tmask, and the new key and value are attended from registers as on sliding. Causality is trivial at L=1. The chunk arithmetic checks out at seq = 80000: chunk = 1280, split 63 has no old keys but holds the new key, so m_max stays finite. At short seq the empty partials get weight 0. ROPE is off on full layers. kv_scale goes through device pointers as on sliding, which a test already covers. Bf16 q is finer than E4M3, so it is allowed. The 512 KB workspace and the shared counters follow config only. The direction claims match TASK.md: only full decode_1 enters the gate, and sliding instantiations compile the same if FULL=False and S<=16 keep static_range, BLOCK_N=64 and num_stages=2. The expected 12-16 us is optimistic, though. LESSONS records that Triton never got past ~2.1 TB/s on this page-size-1 gather (1.3-1.7 TB/s typical), so streaming 20 MB alone takes ~10-13 us. On top of that, the sliding fused kernel already spends 10.3 us on only ~0.5 MB of KV, which means ~7-9 us of fixed prologue, fence, ticket, combine and epilogue cost. A realistic landing is 17-22 us. That is still a gain: at 20 us the decode_1 load goes 1085.8 -> ~960 (1.13x), about +2% on the 6-load geomean. At 14 us it would be ~1.26x on the load. WEAKEST LINK: the proposed runtime range(S) combine for S=64. One CTA would make 2 x 64 serial, dependent L2 round trips of [16,64] fp32 partials. At ~0.2-0.4 us each that is 25-50 us on the critical path and would erase the gain. Keep it unrolled: tl.static_range(64) only costs compile time. Better still, load ws_ml as one [S, M] tile (4 KB) and compute m_max, the weights and l_sum vectorized, then stream acc with independent, unrolled loads. Or use S=32 as the hypothesis itself suggests. Secondary: one program per kv head fetches 64-byte halves of each 128-byte row, so there are twice as many gather requests as in the CUDA split-KV design. That is acceptable at 20 MB.
confounders: sliding-fused-triton-decode1-gate: this change edits the same kernel and the same _sliding_forward launcher, and the two shapes share the _counters(1, 2) buffer. Any sliding decode_1 movement means the edit leaked into the sliding instantiation (FULL=False and S<=16 must keep today's code, BLOCK_N=64 and num_stages=2). That shows up as a per-shape check, not as ambiguity. The shared counter is safe because every launch resets it to 0 and the shapes replay sequentially.

full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv: disjoint gate (batch > 1). The batch==1 test must come before its gate so that full decode_1 never reaches _pre_attention_kernel or FA3. It does not confound the measurement, and cold L2 on each replay removes cache interaction.
paired-heads-launch-cleanup-ab-tune-batch-gate / fa3-hdim128-head-pairing / paired-heads-launch-cleanup: batch 1 already runs unpaired, so the incumbent being replaced is plain FA3. No interaction.
fused-preattention-triton: on this shape it is replaced by _norm_rope plus the in-kernel cache store, the same code sliding decode_1 already validates. Not a confounder.
interference: No companion is needed. The change touches one scored shape (full decode_1) through a config-only gate, and every other shape is byte-identical code. Its effect reads unambiguously from that shape's row and from _sliding_fused_kernel's own time in the profile against the 24.4 us of FA3 main, combine, prepare, pre-attn and norm-gate it replaces. A gain or a loss there can only come from this kernel. An S=32 ab-tune would only be useful as a follow-up if the profile shows the combine dominating, and a single scored submit cannot carry it anyway. Widening _splitkv_gate to batch >= 1 is a competing alternative (79 chunk items over 264 CTAs, 3 launches), not a disambiguating control, so it belongs in the queue as its own hypothesis.
rules_flags: No rule violations found. Every old key in [0, seq-1] plus the new key is attended (no skipping). Bf16 queries are finer than E4M3. KV stays FP8 and the new entries are stored E4M3. Grid, S, BLOCK_N and the workspace come from config only. There are no host syncs, and the counters hold no data derived from inputs.

Scored-submit correctness risk (not a rule break): none of the 16 tests runs full decode at batch 1, so the FULL instantiation is first compiled and checked on a timed call. A compile error, a mask bug or a combine bug there fails the scored run. Mitigation: at import, run an eager self-check like the splitkv one. Use synthetic full-layer inputs at batch 1 with q_len 1, PAGE=1, S=64 and BLOCK_N=128, several seq lengths (e.g. 10, 1025, 80000, and a seq shorter than 64*128 so that many partials are empty), and kv_scale 1 and 0.25. Compare against an FP32 torch reference, and on any error >= 2e-2 or a non-finite output, print a marker and fall back to the master FA3 path. Keep the host syncs inside that import-time check only.
open_questions: Does Triton's pipeliner actually overlap the dependent page-table load with K/V in the runtime range(start, end, 128) loop at num_stages=3 (BLOCK_N=128: 3 stages x 16 KB = 48 KB smem)? If not, ~10 dependent round trips per CTA will set the floor near 10 us on their own.
Would one program per (b, split) covering both kv heads, reading each 128-byte row once, beat two programs per row-half here? The CUDA split-KV design reached ~2.95 TB/s that way.
Is widening _splitkv_gate to batch >= 1 (a one-line change to a kernel that is already self-checked) a cheaper route to the same ~10 us? It would cost 3 launches, against the fused kernel's 1.
Expected 12-16 us versus a realistic 17-22 us: record the replaced kernel's own time and the achieved bandwidth (20.5 MB / kernel time) so a modest gain is not read as a failure.
